Jordan — thanks. Quick answers below, apologies for the roughness:

- Peak minute QPS: 2,100 requests/min (35 requests/sec) — this is for our user-facing chat product. Peak users concentrated between 9–11am PT.
- Avg tokens/response: 280 tokens (median); 95th pct ~1,200 tokens (long multi-step threads)
- Traffic split: interactive chat 85%, embedding/rerank batch 10%, async summarization 5%
- Latency SLO: P95 end-to-end < 1.2s for chat (generation time target <= 900ms), availability target 99.9%

We also have a small but quality-sensitive cohort ("Northfield Pro") — ~10% of traffic — that will require the higher-performance model (we expect to route those to a higher-capacity model variant).

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks for the quick answers. I ran a baseline SLA simulation and put the detailed per-endpoint numbers into the attached workbook (northfield_sla_simulation_v1.xlsx). Key findings / recommendations below — summary only so execs can read quickly:

1) Baseline assumptions used in the sim (documented in worksheet 'Assumptions'):
   - Chat peak: 35 req/sec (2,100 req/min)
   - Avg tokens/chat: 280; P95 tokens/chat: 1,200
   - Redwood runtime measured throughput (continuous batching, A100-class):
       * Redwood-LLM-8B-q4: ~6,800 tokens/sec per GPU (measured with your mix: 85% chat, 15% batch)
       * Redwood-LLM-34B-q4: ~1,900 tokens/sec per GPU (quality variant)
   - Network/overhead multiplier: 1.10 (small E2E overhead)

2) Peak tokens/sec demand (worst-case instant peak using P95 sizes):
   - Chat P95 throughput: 35 req/sec * 1,200 tokens = 42,000 tokens/sec
   - Embedding/rerank batch (concurrent workers): 5 req/sec * 1,500 tokens = 7,500 tokens/sec
   - Summarization async: 2 req/sec * 2,500 tokens = 5,000 tokens/sec
   - Total instantaneous peak (P95 composition): ~54,500 tokens/sec

3) GPU slab sizing (recommendation):
   - Primary slab (serve interactive chat, bulk of traffic) using 8B quantized variant:
       * Measured throughput: 6,800 tokens/sec per GPU → raw GPUs required = 54,500 / 6,800 ≈ 8.0 GPUs
       * Account for 1.10 overhead → 8.8 GPUs → round up to 10 GPUs
       * Add operational headroom (25%) for bursting, model warmup, and degradation handling → provision 12 GPUs on primary slab
   - Quality slab (Northfield Pro cohort routed to 34B variant):
       * Target set to handle 10% of peak traffic → 5,450 tokens/sec demand
       * Per-GPU throughput 1,900 → raw GPUs = 5,450 / 1,900 ≈ 2.9 → overhead + round-up = 4 GPUs
       * Add 25% headroom → provision 5 GPUs on quality slab
   - Suggested dedicated capacity total: 17 GPUs (12 primary + 5 quality)

4) Latency fit / SLO outlook:
   - Based on our measured per-GPU throughput and continuous-batching latency curves, the 12-GPU primary slab yields modeled P95 generation latency ~650–800ms for chat P95 sizes; end-to-end P95 ~850–1,000ms (meets your 1.2s target with 20–30% margin).
   - Quality slab P95 generation latency modeled at ~900–1,100ms (P95), end-to-end ~1.1–1.3s for long tails — recommend trimming long-tail tokenization or enabling streaming fallback to ensure strict 1.2s end-to-end for the Pro cohort if necessary.

5) Operational considerations / fallback policies:
   - Route cold-start or large batched jobs to burst pool (hosted spare capacity) during peaks to avoid throttling.
   - Enable prefix/KV caching for common prompts; we estimate caching could reduce tokens/sec by ~8–12% for Northfield's chat patterns (see 'Caching_Effect' tab).
   - Autoscaling policy: keep slab steady at provisioned GPUs with short-burst autoscale to +30% from hosted capacity to avoid costly overprovisioning on Dedicated.

6) Cost / procurement note (high-level):
   - We can price a 17-GPU dedicated slab with the mix above under a 12-month commitment and include 30% burst credits. Exact commercial terms in attached proposal (northfield_proposal_v3.pdf).

Next steps I propose:
- Samir/Priya: confirm if you want to tighten the P95 latency target for the Pro cohort (we can recalibrate and size).
- Jordan/Rishi: I'll slot this into the pricing draft and produce a variant with a 20-GPU conservative procurement scenario (to include extra headroom for holiday spikes).

Samir — happy to walk through the workbook on a 30-min call this week if helpful.

Thanks,
